pages.text: The sun was sinking behind the hill. The sheep were still scattered across the meadow.
"Today I want to herd them into the pen." Pipo left the pen gate wide open. Mom pulled her straw hat snugly onto her head and said, "I'm counting on you."
Grandpa Sheep came up the hill with his walking stick. "I know all about herding sheep. This is how we did it long ago."
Grandpa banged his stick on the ground. The sheep pricked up their ears.
Bang, bang! Bang, bang! Grandpa banged louder and louder.
The sheep were frightened and ran in every direction. White sheep scattered all over the hill.
Grandpa looked down at his stick and shook the dust off it. His shoulders drooped.
Pipo didn't shout. Pipo walked quietly toward the pen, ahead of all the sheep.
The sheep formed a line behind Pipo. One after another, they followed along.
The last sheep slipped into the pen. Grandpa had found himself standing in line behind it. "Ha, ha! I nearly went in too."
